Given the plots of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ above, find ${h}^{′}(1)$ where $h(x)=\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}.$

${h}^{′}(1)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The quotient rule for derivatives gives

$$
{h}^{′}(x)=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)\cdot g(x)-f(x)\cdot {g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(1)=\frac{{f}^{′}(1)\cdot g(1)-f(1)\cdot {g}^{′}(1)}{(g(1))^{2}}.
$$

From the graphs above, we obtain that $f(1)=2$ and $g(1)=1.$

Additionally:

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (-1,3)$ equals $-\frac{1}{2}.$ So, ${f}^{′}(1)=-\frac{1}{2}.$

- The slope of $g(x)$ on $x\in (0,3)$ equals $-1.$ So, ${g}^{′}(1)=-1.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(1) & =\frac{{f}^{′}(1)\cdot g(1)-f(1)\cdot {g}^{′}(1)}{(g(1))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{1}{2})\cdot 1-2\cdot (-1)}{(1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\frac{3}{2}}{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
